questions.question: How many bits are in an IPv4 address?
questions.explanation: IPv4 addresses are 32 bits long, divided into four 8-bit octets.

questions.question: How many bits are in an IPv6 address?
questions.explanation: IPv6 addresses are 128 bits long, providing a much larger address space than IPv4.

questions.question: Which IP address class has the first octet range 192-223?
questions.explanation: Class C addresses have first octet values from 192 to 223 and are used for small networks.

questions.question: Which private IP address range belongs to Class A?
questions.explanation: 10.0.0.0/8 is the Class A private address range reserved for private networks.

questions.question: What is the default subnet mask for a Class B network?
questions.explanation: Class B networks use 255.255.0.0 as the default subnet mask, providing 16 host bits.

questions.question: What does CIDR stand for?
questions.explanation: CIDR allows flexible allocation of IP addresses without being bound by class boundaries.

questions.question: What is the loopback address in IPv4?
questions.explanation: 127.0.0.1 is the loopback address used for testing network software on the local machine.

questions.question: What type of address is used to send data to all hosts on a network?
questions.explanation: A broadcast address sends data to all devices within a network segment.

questions.question: What does NAT stand for?
questions.explanation: NAT translates private IP addresses to public IP addresses for internet communication.

questions.question: What notation expresses the subnet mask in CIDR?
questions.explanation: CIDR uses slash notation like /24 to indicate the number of network bits in the subnet mask.

questions.question: How many usable host addresses does a /24 network provide?
questions.explanation: A /24 has 256 total addresses minus the network and broadcast addresses, leaving 254 usable.

questions.question: What is the default subnet mask of a Class A network?
questions.explanation: Class A uses a default /8 mask, written 255.0.0.0.

questions.question: Which IP address class is reserved for multicast?
questions.explanation: Class D addresses (224.0.0.0-239.255.255.255) are reserved for multicast groups.

questions.question: Which IP address class is reserved for experimental and research use?
questions.explanation: Class E (240.0.0.0 and above) is reserved for experimental purposes.

questions.question: What does the network portion of an IP address identify?
options: The network a host belongs to
questions.explanation: The network bits identify which network segment a host belongs to.

questions.question: Which address range do hosts self-assign when DHCP fails (APIPA)?
questions.explanation: APIPA assigns link-local addresses in the 169.254.0.0/16 range.

questions.question: What is the first octet range of Class B addresses?
questions.explanation: Class B addresses have a first octet of 128-191.

questions.question: What is the first octet range of Class D addresses?
questions.explanation: Class D multicast addresses span 224-239 in the first octet.

questions.question: Which of the following is a public IP address?
questions.explanation: 8.8.8.8 is public; the other three fall inside RFC 1918 private ranges.

questions.question: What is the CIDR notation for subnet mask 255.255.255.128?
questions.explanation: 255.255.255.128 has 25 consecutive network bits, written as /25.

questions.question: How many host bits remain in a /27 subnet?
questions.explanation: 32 total bits minus 27 network bits leaves 5 host bits.

questions.question: How many usable host addresses does a /30 subnet provide?
questions.explanation: A /30 has 4 addresses minus network and broadcast, leaving 2 for point-to-point links.

questions.question: Which subnet mask is equivalent to /20?
questions.explanation: Twenty network bits gives the mask 255.255.240.0.

questions.question: What does the host portion of an IP address identify?
options: A specific device on a network
questions.explanation: The host bits identify an individual device within the network.

questions.question: What does APIPA stand for?
questions.explanation: APIPA self-assigns a 169.254.x.x address when no DHCP server responds.

questions.question: What does IPv6 use instead of broadcast addresses?
questions.explanation: IPv6 has no broadcast; it uses multicast and anycast instead.
